faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Adastra Sky

items.a: Adastra Sky is an astrotourism platform for the Canary Islands that lets you discover and explore stellar sanctuaries —observation points with exceptional conditions for enjoying the night sky.

It is an astronomical observation point selected for its low light pollution, altitude, accessibility and sky quality. In Adastra Sky you will find observatories, astronomical viewpoints and landscape viewpoints across the 8 islands of the archipelago.

items.q: How is the Bortle scale calculated?
items.a: The Bortle scale rates night-sky quality from 1 to 9, where 1 is a completely dark sky and 9 a heavily light-polluted city sky. Many sanctuaries in the Canary Islands score between 1 and 4.

items.q: How do I explore the sanctuaries?
items.a: Use the interactive map in the «Sky map» section to see every point of interest. You can filter by island, type of sanctuary or Bortle scale. Each point includes altitude, coordinates, accessibility and available facilities.

Adastra is the platform's astronomy assistant. It consults documents from the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias and data tools (weather, zones, ephemerides) and cites the sources it uses. It remembers what you have discussed in the current conversation, so you can ask follow-up questions such as «And from Teide?».

items.q: Can I delete my conversations with Adastra?
items.a: Yes. In the chat, open «Conversations» and click the bin icon next to the conversation you want to delete. Only you can see your conversations.

items.q: How do I plan an observation?
items.a: In «Planner» you choose what you want to see (for example, Saturn) and when. The platform uses real ephemerides to work out when it will be high in the sky, checks the cloud forecast for the best nearby sanctuaries and suggests places and times, always showing the confidence of the result and its limitations.

items.q: Can I save my favourite sanctuaries?
items.a: For now you can explore and discover sanctuaries. A favourites list will be available in a future update.

items.q: Why are the Canary Islands such a special destination?
items.a: Because of their subtropical location, low light pollution protected by the Sky Law, atmospheric stability and two of the world's most important observatories: Roque de los Muchachos (La Palma) and Teide (Tenerife).

items.q: What is the best time of year for stargazing?
items.a: The Canary Islands offer good conditions all year round. Summer usually brings clearer skies and is ideal for the Milky Way; winter offers longer nights. Check the calendar and the planner to choose your night.

Not necessarily. Many objects are visible to the naked eye from a dark sky. For a fuller experience we recommend binoculars or a portable telescope, plus warm clothing: at altitude it gets very cold at night.

The Messier Catalogue, compiled by Charles Messier in the 18th century, lists 110 objects —nebulae, star clusters and galaxies— that he recorded so they would not be confused with comets. Most of them can be seen from the Canary Islands, such as the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), the Orion Nebula (M42) or the Hercules Cluster (M13).

No. The Messier catalogue only includes objects outside the Solar System. The planets visible from the Canary Islands —Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Venus— are observed directly and are not part of the catalogue. Some Messier objects, such as the Pleiades (M45) or the Orion Nebula (M42), are visible to the naked eye from dark skies (Bortle 1-3).

items.q: What is the Global Sky Score?
items.a: It is a general indicator of sky quality across the archipelago, calculated from the Bortle scale of the registered sanctuaries on a 0–10 scale. It describes how dark the sky is, not the weather: it does not guarantee that a given night will be clear.
It is our own 0–100 rating that combines altitude, Bortle scale, estimated seeing, transparency, accessibility and facilities so you can quickly compare observation points.

items.q: What do the Astro, Photo, Tourism and Global categories mean?
items.a: Astro rates visual observation (Bortle, seeing, transparency, altitude, average cloud and humidity). Photo rates astrophotography (landscape quality, orientation, composition, photographer access and Bortle). Tourism rates access, safety and facilities. Global is the weighted average of the three.

items.q: How do I update my profile?
items.a: Go to «Settings» in the side menu, edit your details and click «Save changes».

items.q: How do I change the language?
items.a: In «Settings» you can choose Español, English or Deutsch. The change applies immediately to the whole interface and to Adastra's answers.

items.q: What if I forget my password?
items.a: Contact the team through the «Contact» section to reset your password.
